title: How Transitive Are Real-World Group Interactions? - Measurement and Reproduction

problem.claim: The work studies transitivity in real-world group interactions represented as hypergraphs.

gap.claim: The authors state that real-world group-interaction transitivity had not previously been examined.

contributions.claim: The authors suggest intuitive axioms as necessary characteristics of hypergraph transitivity measures.
The authors propose HyperTrans, a principled hypergraph transitivity measure, together with Fast-HyperTrans for fast computation.
The authors analyze transitivity patterns in real-world and random hypergraphs and propose the scalable generator THera to reproduce observed patterns using community structures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HyperTrans satisfies all proposed axioms.
The authors report that real-world hypergraphs exhibit transitivity patterns distinguishable from those in random hypergraphs.
The authors report that THera reproduces observed transitivity patterns by leveraging community structures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Group interactions among multiple entities are modeled as hypergraphs, motivating the study of transitivity beyond ordinary graphs.
The authors identify a lack of examination of transitivity in real-world group interactions.
The work investigates real-world hypergraph transitivity by proposing axioms, HyperTrans, and Fast-HyperTrans.
The authors compare transitivity patterns in real-world hypergraphs with those in random hypergraphs.
The authors propose THera, a scalable generator intended to reproduce observed patterns through community structures.

source_observation.claim: The authors connect a principled hypergraph transitivity measure to axioms and provide a fast computation algorithm.

interpretation.claim: For a new structural measure, explicit desirable properties can guide definition and implementation.

application.claim: Use axioms to evaluate candidate measures before applying them to real-world relational data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the proposed axioms are sufficient for every intended application.

source_observation.claim: The proposed generator uses community structures to reproduce observed transitivity patterns.

interpretation.claim: Generative models may need to preserve mesoscopic organization to reproduce higher-order interaction patterns.

application.claim: When generating synthetic group-interaction data, incorporate empirically observed community structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which patterns are reproduced or how reproduction is evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the proposed axioms.
The abstract does not describe the HyperTrans formula or Fast-HyperTrans complexity.
The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets or quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the random-hypergraph baselines or comparison protocol.
The abstract does not describe THera's generation procedure or evaluation metrics.
